perf.summary: Dispose nulls each pointer then assigns 'this = default', making the per-field null-out writes dead.
perf.currentCost: Four 'this.X = null;' stores followed by 'this = default;' which zeroes the entire struct (including the just-nulled pointers and Allocator). The intermediate null stores are redundant writes.
perf.proposedChange: Drop the four 'this.Field = null;' assignments; keep the null-checks to decide whether to Free, then a single 'this = default;' clears all pointers and scalars at once. Note 'this = default' also clears Allocator (a get-only auto-prop with a backing field), matching current behavior since the final 'this = default' already does so.
perf.rationale: Removes 4 redundant store instructions; 'this = default' is a single vectorizable block zero of the struct. Net fewer writes on the dispose path.
perf.risk: Behavior identical: the only observable post-state is an all-zero struct. Ensure Free is still called before zeroing (it is, inside each if). 'this = default' already runs today, so clearing Allocator is not a behavior change.
